dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: I was just here for a quick meal — not to have a waiter look down his nose at me for picking the wrong wine to go with my food!

dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: I mean, aren't both Chardon and Corte white wines? Why do people have to make such a hue and cry about something as simple as a meal?

dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: The most infuriating thing is that when I tried to resolve the situation by following his recommendation, not only was the price cheaper, but the flavor really was better than the one I'd picked originally.

dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: I mean, I should've thanked him, but his attitude really was... Darn it.

dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: Why are our legal systems and court processes the way they are?

dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: I've been to other nations, and upon learning their laws, I've come to find our theatrical trials less and less bearable.

dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: Such drama denigrates the law and affects the development of art... What in the world are the higher-ups thinking?

dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: I just feel there are some subtle changes underway with Fontaine's legal systems and judicial processes.

dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: I've been to other nations and studied their systems. And since, I've come to find our theatrical trials less and less bearable.

dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: But I do think there's been less theatrics lately. Our visitors seem to be coming to learn about the law, rather than to see a spectacle.

dialogues.speaker: Eloise
dialogues.text: Or am I wrong? I'll have to keep observing.
